text: Before writing code, the agent pauses to clarify what you're actually trying to accomplish
quote: it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

text: Produces a detailed implementation plan clear enough for a junior engineer to follow, emphasizing TDD, YAGNI and DRY
quote: your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Ar

text: Runs a subagent-driven-development process that dispatches each task to a subagent, which implements and gets reviewed before continuing
quote: this month's cool new process, where it dispatches tasks one by one to subagents to implement and then code reviews each task before continuing.

text: Agent can work autonomously for a couple hours following the plan without deviating
quote: It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

text: Requests are classified as spike/bounded/architectural so small tasks skip the heavyweight two-document planning ritual
quote: Requests are classified as spike, bounded, or architectural; small tasks skip the two-document ritual.

text: Every implementation path still pauses for explicit human approval before work begins
quote: Every path still stops for your approval before implementation.

text: Non-destructive conflicts or ambiguities get an automatic recorded ruling and work continues; only irreversible actions stop for a human
quote: Non-catastrophic conflicts and ambiguities get a recorded ruling and work continues; only destructive or irreversible actions still stop for a human.

text: Small same-shape tasks are batched into a single subagent dispatch to cut cost, with a batch review verifying every planned file landed in the diff
quote: Small same-shape tasks batch into one dispatch, cutting subagent cost sharply on micro-task plans; batch reviews verify every file in the brief made it into the diff.

text: Worktree removal refuses to force-delete uncommitted work; it names the files and asks instead
quote: When `git worktree remove` refuses because the tree holds uncommitted work, the skill stops, names the files, and asks — instead of reaching for `--force`.

text: Each plan now gets its own scoped workspace directory so parallel plans don't misread another plan's progress ledger
quote: a follow-up plan in the same working tree could read the previous plan's ledger as its own progress... `sdd-workspace` now requires the plan file and resolves a per-plan directory

text: The review-fix loop resumes the same implementer across rounds, with a five-round circuit breaker escalating to controller adjudication
quote: The review-fix loop resumes the implementer... installs a five-round circuit breaker with controller adjudication when it trips.

text: Installable into Devin CLI via a single plugin-install command, with skills auto-triggering at session start
quote: **Devin CLI**: `devin plugins install obra/superpowers` now works, and skills auto-trigger at session start.

text: Installable into Hermes Agent from a git clone, registering with Hermes' native skill loader
quote: **Hermes Agent**: install from a git clone; skills register with Hermes' native loader and the bootstrap loads on the first turn.

text: After brainstorming, automatically creates and switches into a git worktree so parallel tasks don't clobber each other
quote: After you're done brainstorming, if you're in a git repo it automatically creates a worktree for the project and changes to that directory. This means that you can start parallel tasks on the same project that don't clobber each other.

text: At the end of implementation, offers to open a GitHub PR, merge the worktree locally, or simply stop
quote: At the end of the implementation process, Claude will now offer to make a GitHub pull request, merge the worktree back to the source branch locally, or just stop.

text: All skills live as plain files under skills/ that are shared verbatim across every supported harness
quote: Skills (harness-agnostic). Everything in `skills/` is the source of truth, shared verbatim by every harness.

text: Skill compliance is tested with a Python harness driving real tmux sessions across Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLI, judged by an LLM verifier
quote: Python harness driving real tmux sessions of Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI, with an LLM actor and verifier judging skill compliance.

text: New skills are built TDD-style: write pressure-test scenarios, watch them fail, write the skill doc, watch tests pass, then refactor to close loopholes
quote: You write test cases (pressure scenarios with subagents), watch them fail (baseline behavior), write the skill (documentation), watch tests pass (agents comply), and refactor (close loopholes).

text: Relevant skills must be invoked before any response or action, including clarifying questions or exploring the codebase
quote: Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files.

text: Enforces true red/green TDD — no production code is written without a failing test first
quote: NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST

text: Provides slash commands like /brainstorming and /execute-plan to run structured design and batched implementation with review checkpoints
quote: Invoke skills with slash commands like `/brainstorming` to explore requirements and design before implementation, or `/execute-plan` to run batched implementation plans with review checkpoints.

text: A debugging safeguard triggers a mandatory architectural review after three failed fix attempts
quote: safeguards that trigger architectural review after three failed fix attempts

text: Ships 20+ pre-built skills plus a skills-search tool for discovering them
quote: 20+ battle-tested skills; `/brainstorm`, `/write-plan`, `/execute-plan` commands; Skills-search tool for discovery; SessionStart context injection

text: Injects skill context automatically at session start with no per-session opt-in required
quote: The harness must let you inject text into the model's context at the start of every session, with no per-session opt-in by your human partner.

text: Includes bash/node/python integration tests for the plugin's own non-LLM code (brainstorm server, plugin loading, sync utilities)
quote: tests/` — does the plugin's non-LLM code work? Bash + node + python integration tests for brainstorm-server JS, OpenCode plugin loading, codex-plugin sync, and analysis utilities.

text: Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all recognize a shared cross-runtime skills folder for install
quote: Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all also recognize `~/.agents/skills/` as a cross-runtime alias.

text: Explicit precedence: user instructions override skills, which in turn override default agent behavior
quote: User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior.

text: Using Superpowers in more than one coding agent requires a separate install per harness
quote: Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

text: In Antigravity, the plugin's session-start hook activates Superpowers from the very first message
quote: Antigravity runs the plugin's session-start hook, so Superpowers is active from the first message. Reinstall with the same command to update.

text: Once installed, skills trigger automatically with no extra setup needed by the user
quote: because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

text: Supporting a new harness only adds a tool-mapping reference and bootstrap injector — it never edits the skill files themselves
quote: Porting adds a tool-mapping reference and a bootstrap injector; it never reaches into `skills/*/SKILL.md` to swap tool names.

text: Installs entirely through the target harness's own install mechanism and never edits the user's own files
quote: Everything ships through the harness's own install mechanism. Never edit the user's files.

text: Grok Build CLI is now supported as an install target
quote: Grok Build CLI added to the install docs.

text: A guide documents how to add a new harness (IDE/CLI/agent runner) so skills auto-trigger there like they do natively
quote: This guide explains how to add support for a new harness ... so that Superpowers skills auto-trigger there the same way they do natively.

text: A dedicated writing-skills module teaches the agent to author and test new skills
quote: The writing-skills module teaches you to author and test new skills

text: A one-line marketplace command installs the whole skill collection into Claude Code
quote:
/plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
/plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

text: Plans carry a pointer to a spec document so conflicts get resolved against the design instead of guessed at
quote: Plans carry a `Spec:` pointer and SDD reads the spec at setup, so plan conflicts get resolved against the design instead of guessed at.

text: A code-reviewer agent evaluates each implementation against the plan, coding standards, and architectural principles
quote: The framework includes a code-reviewer agent that evaluates implementations against plans, coding standards, and architectural principles.

text: A four-phase debugging methodology requires root-cause investigation before any fix is applied
quote: a four-phase debugging methodology that requires root cause investigation before any fixes

text: Implementer and reviewer subagents are barred from spawning their own subagents, preventing duplicate reviews
quote: Implementers and reviewers may not spawn their own subagents, which was producing duplicate reviews.

text: Offers a choice between a manual human-PM-style review process or an automated subagent dispatch-and-review process
quote: it offers you a choice between: 1. last month's process (where you'd open a second `claude` session and act as a human PM...) 2. this month's cool new process, where it dispatches tasks one by one to subagents to implement and then code rev
